definitions.explanation: Tension or conflict in relationships between people, groups, or nations. Implies ongoing difficulty rather than a single dispute.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}の{軋轢|あつれき}
{意見|いけん}の{違|ちが}いから{軋轢|あつれき}が{生|しょう}じた。
examples.english: Friction arose from differences of opinion.

examples.japanese: {経営陣|けいえいじん}と{労働組合|ろうどうくみあい}の{間|あいだ}に{軋轢|あつれき}があるらしい。
examples.english: There seems to be friction between management and the labor union.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: Originally refers to the creaking/grinding sound of wheels ({軋|きし}む = to creak, {轢|れき} = wheel). The metaphor extends to interpersonal friction.

FORMALITY: Somewhat formal. Common in news and written language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {軋轢|あつれき}が{生|しょう}じる/{起|お}きる (friction arises)
- {軋轢|あつれき}を{生|う}む (to create friction)
- {軋轢|あつれき}を{避|さ}ける (to avoid friction)
- ～との{軋轢|あつれき} (friction with ~)

RELATED WORDS:
- {摩擦|まさつ} (friction - also metaphorical, more common)
- {対立|たいりつ} (confrontation, opposition)
- {不和|ふわ} (discord, disharmony)
